speakers: Nick Balters (Goldman Sachs, QIS / systematic strategies)
Morris Seabirds (host, standing in for Niels Kaastrup-Larsen)
summary: Late Oct 2025 systematic investor episode. Opens with trend-following performance (April 2025 V-shape whipsaw, speed as the driver of dispersion). Main topic: the roughly $1.3 trillion QIS (bank and asset-manager risk-premia index) market: size, reporting caveats, clients, thousands of indices, wrappers, data-mining control, and whether crowding erodes premia (commodity roll congestion decayed, vol selling insurance-like, trend benefits from early crowding).

coverage.note: Oct 2025 performance numbers; equities dominance; precious metals and livestock give-back
trend attribution by asset class; April V-shape and speed
trend exits in April; QIS size survey
size reporting conventions, double counting, asset class split
survey caveats, substitution effect, clients history
client types, QIS as rules-based index technology
intraday strategies, four pillars of product development
wrappers, options on negatively skewed profiles, vol targeting
vol targeting vs recovery, scale and capacity
innovation versus data mining, product culture
explaining underperformance, crowding question, commodity congestion setup
congestion premium decay, risk-sharing versus allocation premia
insurance premium crowding, trend crowding, externalities

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: this year has been pretty much like a bit of a debate between fragility and resilience, right?
claims.claim: In 2025 the equity market kept absorbing negative news (events against sentiment and growth) and stayed resilient, leaving a fragile-versus-resilient pendulum into November.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: The sharp ratio of the S&P 500 has now decoupled from everything else.
claims.claim: The S&P 500's Sharpe ratio in 2025 was far above every other asset and CTA index (S&P about +18% YTD, MSCI World +22%, BTop50 +2.35%, trend index about flat) as of 29 October 2025.
claims.indicator: BTop50, SG CTA, SG Trend, MSCI World, S&P 500 YTD returns

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: the equity risk premium or you expect to make six seven eight something like that percent per year
claims.claim: The long-run equity premium is about 6-8% a year, but the last five years delivered 15-20% annually except 2022 (inflation spike where equities and rates sold off together).

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: And then a lot of give back of open trade profits uh on exactly these markets.
claims.claim: In October 2025 trend followers gained from long precious metals and livestock until about 20 October, then gave back open profits as palladium, gold, silver, platinum and cattle reversed.
claims.direction: long metals and cattle, then reversal

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: rates keep on being the same story for the year. Keep on whipsing, keep on losing on the trend side.
claims.claim: In 2025 fixed income was the main whipsaw for trend followers, offset by gains in equities, gold, aluminium, copper and a sugar short.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: I think that's the main driver of dispersion that we've seen this year in the trend following space.
claims.claim: The speed of response around the April 2025 equity V-shape (sell-off then recovery) explains most 2025 trend-follower dispersion, worth about 10% for the year.
claims.testable: yes - compare fast and slow trend lookbacks over Apr-Dec 2025

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the short-term traders actually doing well in the Vshape
claims.claim: Fast short-term trend systems captured the V-shape in April, slow systems rode the whole V and recovered, and mid-speed systems got whipsawed at the worst time.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: All the European indices, we we just lost all our own positions in April.
claims.claim: Long-term trend system was stopped out of nearly all equity indices in April 2025 and re-entered only by July-August, so a slow exit/re-entry cost much of the year.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: we're not forcing ourselves to reverse the position into shorts.
claims.claim: Exits go to flat (neutral zone with no-trade area) rather than reversing into a short, so after a stop-out the system waits for a new trend signal.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: they have hit a new all-time high at about$1,300 billion US
claims.claim: Alborne's H1 2025 survey puts QIS notional assets at about $1.3 trillion, split roughly 50/50 between bank and asset-manager QIS.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: fixed income is only 50 billion even though fixed income markets are gigantically large markets
claims.claim: QIS assets are over half equity, then multi-asset and commodities; fixed income (about $50bn), FX ($27bn) and credit ($13bn) are small relative to their market size.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: Do you do a look through leverage adjustment? Do you do delta adjustment if that is an option?
claims.claim: QIS size figures are uncertain because notional is reported inconsistently (unfunded swaps vs options, leverage and delta adjustment) and asset-manager and bank numbers may double count.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the brokilla sum which is close to the 600 billion mark
claims.claim: Broker-dealer QIS is about $600bn plus or minus $100bn on a rough estimate; the market grew with winter periods around 2018 and 2021.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the equity long only space is by far dominating the asset manager world
claims.claim: On the asset-manager side QIS is mainly equity long-only smart beta, while bank QIS is more evenly split and multi-asset/cross-asset carry baskets are growing.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the market still consumes the same level of liquidity demand. it's just now marked under the QIS kind of badge
claims.claim: Part of QIS growth is substitution: exposure that was in a CDA or swap is repackaged as a QIS index, not genuine new strategy demand.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: done by some of the Nordic pensions to replace or maybe enhance um their risk profile by by risk factors
claims.claim: QIS began with commodity roll indices and post-GFC factor investing by Nordic pensions that replaced asset-class mixes with factor mixes (equity market neutral, vol carry).

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: if today we claim that volatility is rewarded and whoever is willing to sell insurance should be compensated that in itself can be described with a set of rules by selling some options
claims.claim: A risk premium (volatility, equity, commodity carry) can be expressed as rules and wrapped as an index or swap, giving investors access like a futures contract on S&P 500.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: utilize their internal models on timing utilize their internal models on sizing focus more on kind of bringing their alpha which is more of a timing element
claims.claim: Clients use QIS for implementation and add their own value through timing and sizing models.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: if the bank can you know kind of like every five minutes or what it is do like a a vulcar intraday strategy on the S&P 500 then I might be better off just buying it from them
claims.claim: Hedge funds buy intraday momentum and vol strategies from banks through QIS because the operational and technology burden is high.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: a combination of four main pillars in terms of product development
claims.claim: QIS development has four drivers: academic research, shifting client appetite from hedge fund replacement to specific outcomes (defensive, yield, inflation, regime), technology, and market evolution (new commodities, listed short options).

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: allowing us to almost do out of sample testing on universes that otherwise would not be able to do so
claims.claim: New tradable markets (frontier commodities, listed options) allow out-of-sample tests net of cost on universes that could not be tested before.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: any different implementation be it for a specific client ask or a specific need has to be a different index
claims.claim: There are thousands of QIS indices mostly because of client customisation (tax treatment net vs gross total return, no equity upside, portfolio exclusions) not because designers kept replacing indices after overfitting.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the vast majority has always been in the in the kind of the delta 1 space
claims.claim: Most QIS volume is delta-1 swap exposure; optionalised wrappers (call options capping losses) are a small share, rising in the last two to three years mainly from insurers.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: almost writing a call option to it in itself nullifies the existence of the premium in the first place
claims.claim: Buying a call on a short-vol carry index removes the premium, since the premium compensates for the occasional vol spike risk; banks quoting such options need vol control and sell at wider premia.
claims.indicator: call option on volatility carry index

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: negative skew in equity momentum can be moderated by uh by vault targeting
claims.claim: Equity momentum is vol-targeted, which reduces its negative skew and makes option pricing on top easier.
claims.testable: yes - backtest with and without vol target

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: if you were to volatility target a strategy that is supposed to be reacting and recovering post the volatility spike you're kind of acting against its ability to recover
claims.claim: Volatility targeting hurts strategies that recover after volatility spikes (rebounds), because it cuts exposure when the rebound starts, so options-friendly vol-targeting can be suboptimal.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: if there is a liquidity premium to be harvested or illiquidity or whatever it's worth it
claims.claim: Illiquid and frontier markets may offer higher premia but have lower capacity; QIS design is conscious of capacity and nothing is built for infinite scale.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: so there are multiple cases whereby a specific design cannot sustain anymore without being market impactful
claims.claim: Banks can close an index when a design can no longer be run without market impact, unlike an ETF.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: there is no way you can avoid data mining. If I were to show you like 10 back tests, you would basically drop the bottom one
claims.claim: Data mining cannot be avoided; its control is product culture: call it out, look at tweaks as data-mined, and ensure new tweaks are not designed to make the Sharpe look better after a drawdown.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: if only we're a bit slower or if only we're a bit uh I don't know overweight this asset class
claims.claim: After a drawdown (April trend following) there is temptation to tweak speed or sizing, which is an overfitting bias; strategy changes should be justified by explaining, not repairing, recent performance.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: if we cannot explain underperformance that's the worst thing that can happen
claims.claim: Explainable underperformance builds client trust; unexplained underperformance is worst.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: reacting on the motion and just making the last draw down outperform is purely the recipe for underperformance
claims.claim: Reacting to SVB, the dollar-yen unwind and April by tweaking systems to avoid the last drawdown is a recipe for underperformance.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: providing liquidity during that role and then reversing the position you know 5 days later I think that strategy has largely decayed
claims.claim: The commodity index roll (days 5-9) liquidity provision trade worked 10-15 years ago but has largely decayed.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: I capture what is called the congestion premium which is nothing more than liquidity premium liquidity provision here
claims.claim: Congestion trade: pre-position before predictable benchmark commodity index rolls and capture a liquidity premium from passive rolling demand.
claims.direction: buy before benchmark buys, sell before benchmark sells

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: And the flattening out of the strategy, it's more that the initial demand for this liquidity is no longer there.
claims.claim: The congestion trade flattened around 2015-18 not because QIS crowded it (which would give negative returns) but because the market became elastic as passive roll demand shrank; it came back in 2022 with commodity demand.
claims.conditions: returns when passive roll demand is large

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: this demand for commodity roles is not driven by some sort of risk sharing mechanism. It's purely allocation decision.
claims.claim: Allocation-driven premia (roll congestion) can disappear with crowding or lack of demand; risk-sharing premia like volatility selling persist because someone must take the risk others will not.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: the premium to insure your car is going to drop purely by the by the economics of competition
claims.claim: Crowding in an insurance-type premium (vol selling) lowers returns but not to zero because a barrier to entry rises as returns fall, so premia stay positive.

claims.speaker: Morris Seabirds
claims.quote: trend following is actually benefiting from early crowding
claims.claim: Behavioural strategies like trend following may benefit from early crowding; their issue is controlling negative skew events, not premium erosion.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: maybe the cost of care of maintaining this defensive strategy has kind of increased over the years
claims.claim: Intraday momentum became crowded via QIS wrappers in 2021-2022: the defensive payoff remains but its cost of carry rose.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: those components now can expost realize correlations that we haven't seen in a back test.
claims.claim: The main crowding risk is externalities: many investors with similar 60/40 plus overlay products react to the same macro signals and deleverage together, creating correlations not seen in backtests.

claims.speaker: Nick Balters
claims.quote: If your indices do not perform, if they do not provide the premium um that you know we suggest or expect there to be, then the volume will dry up.
claims.claim: Flows follow index performance: if QIS indices fail to deliver the premium, volume dries up and flows revert.
